subject: Using the predict function to produce raster outputs from my top ranked model. Odd output?

messages.author: c30c9e29d10d3cd7
messages.subject: Using the predict function to produce raster outputs from my top ranked model. Odd output?
parts:
Hi

I used the predict function to produce raster outputs from my top ranked model. (code below). This model has good fit according to the Tukeytest.
However, I am confused about the output (see below). I do not understand the scale of the output.
Since I standardized the covariates during the modelling process, i transformed the country-wide data using the same values.
Do you need to back-transform these values to get density values?

Thanks,

I




WWL <-gdistsamp(lambdaformula = ~riv + lake + prec + temp, phiformula = ~1,
    pformula = ~OBS, data = umf, keyfun = "exp", output = "density",
    unitsOut = "kmsq", mixture = "NB")


Abundance:



Estimate SE z P(>|z|)
(Intercept) 10.4275 1.02048 10.22 1.64E-24
riv -6.7359 0.69716 -9.66 4.38E-22
lake -2.4122 0.21556 -11.19 4.56E-29
prec -0.0218 0.00307 -7.1 1.21E-12
temp -0.0121 0.00645 -1.87 6.09E-02





Detection:



Estimate SE z P(>|z|)
(Intercept) 3.709 0.0334 110.9 0.00E+00
OBSSINGLE -0.201 0.0428 -4.7 2.65E-06





Dispersion:



Estimate SE z P(>|z|)

-1.81 0.0662 -27.3 7.80E-164





AIC: 4900.029





layers <- list.files(pattern="tif$", full.names=FALSE)
layers

#stackkazc10a_Clip=river
#stackkazc12a_Clip=lake
#stackkazc2a_clipNDVI=
#stackkazc4a_Clip=temp
#stackkazc6a_Clip=prec
#stackkazc8a_Clip=elevation

#create four raster objects (coordinate system already specified).
riv <- raster("stackkazc10a_Clip.tif")
lake<- raster("stackkazc12a_Clip.tif")
prec<- raster("stackkazc6a_Clip.tif")
temp<- raster("stackkazc4a_Clip.tif")

sc.s # data set for the scaled variables
attributes (sc.s)

#$`scaled:center`
#       ndvi        temp        prec         ele         riv         set        lake  Activefire    firefreq    Firecomb
#107.7638431  58.2120523 205.3780557 253.4246731   0.1981767   0.2733345   0.4512685   0.1569073   0.2029562   0.3013076

#$`scaled:scale`
#       ndvi        temp        prec         ele         riv         set        lake  Activefire    firefreq    Firecomb
# 24.1685758  19.7543778  53.1457608 146.3752595   0.2406652   0.2432223   0.4376988   0.5063272   0.5228263   0.6559030

#Since we standardized the covariates during the modelling process, we transformed the country-wide data using the same values

riv.s <- (riv-0.1981767)/0.2406652
lake.s <- (lake-0.4512685)/0.4376988
prec.s <- (prec-205.3780557)/53.1457608
temp.s <- (temp-58.2120523)/19.7543778

habitat <- stack(riv.s, lake.s, prec.s, temp.s)
names(habitat) <- c("riv", "lake", "prec", "temp")

res(habitat)
extent(habitat)
projection(habitat)
habitat


plot(stack, col=terrain.colors(100))

WWL.density <- predict(WWL, type="lambda", newdata=habitat)
plot(WWL.density, axes=FALSE, col=terrain.colors(100))

messages.author: 4a635fe980c8c1cd
messages.subject: Re: Using the predict function to produce raster outputs from my top ranked model. Odd output?
parts:
Hi,

It is predicting values on the real scale: exp(b0+b1x1....etc.), or expected number of individuals per square km.  The estimated intercept is pretty large (10.425), which corresponds to about 22,000 things per square km in a completely average site. Scaling the predictors to align with the values used during fitting makes sense. If the pixels are smaller than a square km, though, then what is predicted is not the expected N for a pixel, but the expected N if that pixel were a square km.  You can transform the point estimate pretty easily using multiplication (ie., predicted N times the pixel size in square km), although SE would be a little trickier (maybe somebody has code). 

Cheers,

John

messages.author: 4a635fe980c8c1cd
messages.subject: Re: Using the predict function to produce raster outputs from my top ranked model. Odd output?
parts:
I don't think so. The raster may be projected in a degree-based manner, but the cell size or resolution of the raster can't be degree-based, or pixel size would be variable.  The resolution for land-cover depends upon the satellite recording the reflectance, but the cell-size is commonly somewhere between 30 meters x 30 meters (which is, uh, 0.0009 sq. km?)  and 250 meters x 250 meters (or 0.0625 sq. km)....interpolated layers like DEM's or precipitation type typically fall in the same general range.

I should have thought of this before, but if you have Marc and Andy's 2016 book, page 442 or thereabouts walks through raster prediction--using an offset for area, setting output="abund", and including a static area value for the raster cell size allows the predict function to do all of the delta method standard error estimation for you.

Cheers,

John

I was thinking that the higher then expected values might be because my rasters are in degrees?
Could that be possible?
